Create original Coop Chaos game concept art, an art-director exploration, NOT a screenshot or finished runtime asset. Use the supplied reference only for painterly sculpted 3D styling, golden sunlight, warm ochre bark, rich moss-green foliage, confident broad planes and small expressive chickens. Completely redesign the tree architecture. No UI, no humans, no human cottages, no roads, no pasted medieval village, no literal face on tree. Trees express personality through posture, bark folds, scars and asymmetry. Buildings are woven by intelligent personified chickens using twigs, reeds, nesting grass, forked timber, beak-tied lashings. Keep real-looking chicken bodies, no hands or clothes. Strong crafted shape design, exquisite soft light and contact shadows, material richness without noisy microdetail. High resolution landscape presentation. Text only where requested, elegant small editorial lettering.
BOARD 1 — title 'MORROW / THE TREE BEFORE THE TOWN'. A beautiful professional concept sheet with TWO large equal-size matched-angle three-quarter elevated views of precisely the SAME great oak, full roots and full crown inside frame, warm pale parchment background. LEFT: completely unbuilt living oak, architectural anatomy naturally revealed; RIGHT: same oak lightly inhabited with just three organic additions. The tree has a low heavy trunk twisting slowly counterclockwise, deep honey-brown fluting flowing continuously from broad roots into 3 massive unequal ascending boughs, a high fork shaped like an open hand, older healed knots, moss in shady creases. One very long elbowing bough makes a generous low east-facing porch; another climbs diagonally behind to a protected middle fork; a third leans out to a high watch perch. Do NOT make evenly stacked floors or a cylindrical tower. Crown is lush and substantial: four broad irregular scalloped masses, each connected to visible tapering twigs; foliage chiefly above and behind the inhabited side, with organic blue-sky windows between boughs. Branches visible because of their actual shape and viewpoint, not a cutaway tree. On left mark six small, tasteful leader labels: 'Root court', 'Hauling cleft', 'Low fork', 'Quiet bough', 'Crown window', 'Watch tip'. Chickens provide scale: crown about 16 chicken heights tall, trunk about 3 chicken widths. On right root court has a reed bundle and two working hens; a clearly unobstructed vertical basket lift passes through the gap beside trunk to a branch-supported landing with a pulley mounted on a strong fork, a woven covered nest-home fits around the low elbow, and an open communal perch fits the middle fork. Everything physically connected, roofs do not hide the supporting branches; whole unbuilt tree is still identifiable. Tiny perched birds in crown, one on natural limb. Sell the BEAUTY of branch volume, branch junctions and layered foliage, with tree doing 80percent of the silhouette and buildings20percent. No regimented collection of circular decks. Bottom tiny subtitle 'Anatomy first. A kingdom grows into it.'

BOARD 2 — title 'LIFE BETWEEN THE BOUGHS'. An extraordinary art-direction detail sheet, THREE generous connected visual vignettes on warm ivory, restrained hairline separations, equal visual importance. Each is a close elevated three-quarter dollhouse view of an inhabited part of the SAME great oak, enough surrounding live bark and real branches to demonstrate construction connection. LEFT label 'THE WORKING ROOTS': broad buttress roots shape a ground gathering and weaving court, loose reed bundles sorted into woven cradles, an open basket loading bay between two roots, two hens manipulate a long reed with beaks and feet, a small rooster watches clearing, one sturdy trunk ladder lands on a lower branch platform. Show vertical cargo basket route in the open cleft beside trunk, not passing through wood. MIDDLE label 'THE BRANCH NEIGHBORHOOD': a genuinely massive sloping limb rises from trunk lower left to upper right; three different modest woven interventions follow its changing angle: one crescent communal floor braced at a fork, a shaded oval sleeping hood nestling on branch, a sunny small seed drying rack at outer end. Platforms curved to wood, wide tied saddles and braces, no drilled metal bolts, no magically floating decks. A stout natural limb stays the main walking spine with uneven beak-made gripping strips and short connecting ladders; quiet nest entrances separated from busy turning space. A hen carries reed cargo from lift unloading lip at trunk, another rests half asleep, chicks visible in future sheltered nursery; these are future concept activities. RIGHT label 'THE HAULING WINDOW': show whole physically plausible chicken-built counterweight cargo rig from ground loading basket to high branch landing with leafy canopy above. One thick curved bough takes load, a fork supports a wooden pulley, rope clearly runs over wheel to suspended stone counterweight in its own separate clear shaft, the basket is held by two guides to prevent wild swing. Both end platforms with room to transfer cargo, an operating perch where a hen uses body weight to pull rope. Cargo basket EMPTY of passengers; small twig safety gate at landing. Beautiful dappled light revealing wooden fibers, broad planes, tied joints, loose feather and remembered wear. Keep mechanisms simple and readable, chicken-scale in all3vignettes. Functional branch joints more important than embellishment. No human furniture, gears everywhere or architecture disconnected from tree. This board is a visually convincing concept, not an engineering blueprint.

BOARD 3 — title 'A KINGDOM WITH ROOM TO BREATHE'. A breathtaking single wide elevated 2.5D strategy-game concept scene, sufficiently high viewpoint (about40degrees down) to see platforms, ground and entire hero crown. Compose a mature great oak kingdom on left-center beside a willow neighbor at right riverbank; a pair of pale birches behind; golden productive meadow opens toward viewer. Full hero oak roots and crown in frame with generous negative space around silhouette. The oak is the main character: low twisted muscular trunk, 3different sweeping limbs and broad layered rich green crown, sunlit olive and ochre upper leaves, cool deep undersides; substantial organic windows between asymmetrical leafy crowns reveal inhabited branch forks. NO solid opaque foliage lid. ONLY five purposeful architectural additions on oak: low cozy sleeping home, busy root supply court, midlevel crescent communal terrace integrated in fork, upper quiet woven nest hood, one clearly visible basket lift in open trunk cleft with actual ground loading and branch unloading spaces. A branching natural-wood spine and short crooked ladders connect, do not wrap every trunk in uniform spiral platforms. Keep bark visible throughout. Neighboring willow has slimmer arching stems, hanging golden-green foliage curtains framing a low light woven veranda; one short sagging woven bridge with credible anchors connects opposite outward boughs of oak and willow, no arbitrary floating bridge. Birch has a tiny airy lookout perch, no heavy tower. In the meadow chickens scratch for insects, drag grass and carry small bundles; show7or8distinct chickens large enough to read, plus a couple resting in branch spaces; no crowds of microscopic birds. Ground vegetation comes in purposeful lush masses and bare activity patches, no constructed roads. Creek glints and reeds on bank. Warm late-afternoon lighting with shafts through crown windows, moss, bark ridges, beautifully shaped stone, soft contact shadows, polished painterly 3D concept aesthetic. An inhabited tree must still read first as an exquisite living tree, second as a village. Not an enormous fantasy metropolis, no huts carpeting every inch, no glowing magic, no humanoid walking trees. Tiny subtitle 'Different trees. Shared work. Places worth belonging to.'
refinement: Refine this Coop Chaos tree kingdom CONCEPT image into an actual useful GAME CAMERA ART STUDY. Retain its beautiful sculptural honey bark, rich layered green crown, charming woven nest homes, branch terraces, distinct oak and willow, cute natural chicken bodies, and warm golden lighting. IMPORTANT CHANGES: pull camera substantially backward and raise it to an elevated orthographic strategy view looking down at 40 degrees; the COMPLETE crown of the main oak and all its roots must fit inside the image with generous margin above and left, no cropping any part of its silhouette; reduce immense tree to about16chickenheights, with chickens large enough to read. Landscape wide image. Tree entirely contained in central70percent of image height, with golden meadow foreground and distant woodland behind; composition like a polished beautiful 2.5D playable diorama, not low cinematic camera. Do not obscure all the visible boughs when raising camera: intelligently arrange crown into broad irregular layered leaf clouds AROUND the rear and outer load-bearing boughs, organic daylight windows onto the front fork terraces. Keep enough living foliage that it looks like a healthy old oak, not a stripped bonsai or cutaway. Three strong unequal tapering limbs with clear continuous junctions into a crooked fluted trunk. Preserve a readable low natural roost, an empty future buildable fork and quiet upper perch in addition to buildings; not every branch occupied. Main oak buildings limited to low woven sleep hood, modest crescent shared fork court, high private nest, ground reed storage. Working goods basket beside trunk: carries reeds ONLY, no passenger chicken. Cargo path clear from ground to unloading landing, support/pulley at strong fork, separate rope counterweight; no basket intersects trunk. Ground chicken visible with bundle. Short narrow woven bridge to nearby willow branch at SAME HEIGHT and visually real endpoints, willow with light veranda. Birch silhouette behind left. No built paths or roads; ground has natural irregular activity patches only. Remove existing large typography; only small elegant title at bottom-left 'MORROW / A LIVING CANOPY', with tiny caption 'Elevated camera concept — unbuilt branches remain part of the kingdom'. NO UI or fake game screenshot, this remains concept art. Rich believable soft cast shadows, warm rim light, dappled canopy shade and varied bark surfaces. Match original craft quality while prioritizing whole-tree and branch readability.
